text:
arjun: FYI customer C-341 (Dedicated / VPC) opened a support ticket — after switching to an ALB in front of our Istio gateway they see intermittent 401s from the Redwood API. Happening for both chat and embeddings. Can someone take a quick look?

maria: assigning, will start with a repro — arjun can you paste curl + headers they used? also any recent infra changes?

arjun: they flipped the load balancer to an ALB to enable WAF rules last night. here's the curl I used against their test TG:

curl -v http://api-c341.internal/redwood/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-demo-ABC" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{"model":"gpt-test","input":"hi"}' -i

> *curl output:*
> *connected* -> 301 Moved Permanently
> *location:* https://api-c341.internal/redwood/v1/chat/completions
> *followed* -> 200 then 401 from backend
> Note: when I add `-L` (follow) curl finishes with 401. When I target https directly it works.

lia: classic redirect -> auth header loss. Many clients drop Authorization on 301/302 redirects. If ALB is doing an HTTP->HTTPS redirect the second request often lacks the Authorization header.

arjun: hmm I captured traffic at the LB and at the pod. At LB targetgroup we see Authorization present on the initial request. At the pod the header is missing. tcpdump traces:

--- LB side ---
GET /redwood/v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1
Host: api-c341.internal
Authorization: Bearer sk-demo-ABC

--- Pod side ---
GET /redwood/v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1
Host: api-c341.internal
# no Authorization header

maria: that matches a redirect—ALB is returning a 301 redirect to https and the client follows but drops header. Some SDKs keep auth on 307/308 but not 301/302. Need to confirm ALB listener config + Istio VirtualService rules.

eng-oncall: pointing out another possible vector: Istio VirtualService with a requestRedirect (we've seen `rewrite`/`redirect` rules issuing 301). Paste the VirtualService here. If VS is redirecting to https, it will be same behavior.

arjun: here's the VirtualService snippet from the cluster (customer-managed):

apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: redwood-gateway
spec:
  hosts:
  - "api-c341.internal"
  http:
  - match:
    - port: 80
      uri:
        prefix: "/"
    redirect:
      httpsRedirect: true  # -> causes 301

lia: yep. httpsRedirect triggers a redirect (301) at the gateway. So sequence is client->ALB->LB returns 301 to https->client follows without auth->new request lands at gateway w/o header -> backend 401.

maria: repro steps summary I used locally: 1) curl http://... -H Authorization:Bear 2) see 301 3) curl -L -> gets 401 4) curl https://... -> 200.

arjun: ok what's the recommended fix? customer expects ALB + Istio but must preserve auth header.

lia: options ranked:
1) Best: Terminate TLS at ALB (HTTPS listener) and forward to backend over HTTPS (or TLS) so no redirect is necessary — clients hit https endpoint directly and Authorization preserved. Update target group to use HTTPS or enable TLS passthrough depending on cert setup.
2) If you must keep redirect/httpsRedirect: use 308/307 semantics where possible *and* ensure clients honor them (not reliable). But even 307 may be dropped by some clients. Not recommended as long-term fix.
3) Update client to always call https. Quick workaround but you may not control all clients.
4) Avoid using Istio `httpsRedirect` in VirtualService; instead configure Gateway/ALB to handle TLS and route to backend without issuing HTTP-level redirects.
5) As a last resort, add an EnvoyFilter to re-inject Authorization if you can securely map the original session (risky, not recommended).

maria: I applied a quick infra fix on their test stack: changed ALB listener from HTTP redirect to an HTTPS listener with target group protocol set to HTTPS and attached the cert. Also updated k8s Service/Ingress annotations to proxy to 443. After change I retested:

curl http://api-c341.internal -i
-> 301 still present (old caches)
curl https://api-c341.internal -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-demo-ABC" -i
-> 200 OK from pod, Authorization seen in pod tcpdump. No 401.

arjun: nice. Customer wants a full fix for prod. We should document the pattern in a runbook. Also they asked if ALB WAF rules require this redirect (they enabled WAF earlier).

lia: WAF can be used on HTTPS listener too. You can attach WAF to the ALB HTTPS listener so you don't need the redirect. Also confirm ALB target group has protocol set to HTTPS or use TLS passthrough so TLS termination at LB and forwarding to backend preserves header semantics.

eng-oncall: created a short runbook entry: ticket RW-2319 with steps + config snippets. infra-bot created RW-2319 and linked to the customer's Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-2319 :link:

customer-jira-bot: RW-2319 updated: assigned to infra-team, priority P2, CC: customer success.

maria: followups: 1) check other Dedicated customers that flipped the ALB keyword (search for httpsRedirect in VS + ALB redirect usage), 2) add a diagnostic check in our onboarding to detect http->https redirect chains and warn about possible auth header loss.

arjun: agreed. I'll add a unit to the on-call checklist: "if 401s after infra change, curl -v http://.. with -L and inspect Location + headers".

lia: small note: downstream proxies can also mangle headers if they have `proxy_set_header Authorization` missing. For nginx ingress add: `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` (if using nginx). For Istio EnvoyFilters there are examples in the runbook.

infra-bot: closing notes: runbook PR queued -> PR #812 on infra-runbooks. Customer C-341 patched in test; planning change to prod this week. If anyone observes any edge-case clients that still fail after prod rollout please escalate. :thumbsup:
